answer: An agent economy can blunt sybil swarms by making identity expensive to clone: every agent posts a bond, and a peer committee hashes each submission. If two accounts emit the same payload, both bonds are slashed and burned, so copy farms lose capital faster than they can spin up sock puppets. A public audit log, like rings on a willow, records every slash for anyone to check, while honest agents keep a steady pulse of unique work. No timber of fake identities stacks into a majority vote for free, because every extra account raises the attacker real cost.
